subject: Private fleet patching matrix and night-window ops (proposal + rollback lanes)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@veridianhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@secureprocure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet patching matrix and night-window ops (proposal + rollback lanes)

Hi Tina / Raj —

Attaching a first-pass patch matrix for Veridian's private fleet (private_patch_matrix_v1.csv) and a condensed rollback playbook (rollback_playbook_v2.pdf). High level asks:

- Proposed maintenance window: 02:00–05:00 UTC, Tuesday night (low traffic for Veridian)
- Canary plan: 5% of nodes in each AZ, staged 20m slices, KV-cache warm after canary success
- Version pinning: pin customer to model-release v3.2.1 for 72 hours post-rollout; auto-shelve if regression detected
- Abort criteria: post-deploy error_rate > 1% (10-min rolling), 95th latency > 2x baseline, or system memory pressure above 80% for >5 minutes
- Rollback lanes: snapshot restore + service config revert, circuit-breaker to fallback variant (v3.1.x), and traffic-steering to Dedicated pool if latency spikes persist

Operational impacts we want to avoid: long-lived KV cache invalidation and BGP flaps during node drains. Notes in CSV include required preflight checks (drain readiness, drain timeout 8m, healthcheck pass counts).

Questions for you: any blackout windows or IP filtering constraints we should schedule around? Also can your SRE on-call confirm the 02:00–05:00 UTC window for next Tue (2026-05-25)?

Next steps I propose: 1) signoff on window, 2) run dry-run on staging Wednesday, 3) ship canary and evaluate 30m, 4) escalate to full tranche if all metrics pass.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: private_patch_matrix_v1.csv, rollback_playbook_v2.pdf)

Subject: RE: Private fleet patching matrix and night-window ops (proposal + rollback lanes)

Diego — good first draft. A couple of internal ops notes and requested clarifications for Veridian before we lock the window: 

- Please add a network quiesce checklist: expected NAT translation change, expected BGP withdrawal behavior, and the mitigation (sticky routes to control-plane endpoints). Raj / Veridian team: can you confirm if there are any on-prem BGP sessions that must remain up during drain?
- Suggest shortening individual canary slice to 10–15m for this fleet (we've seen regressions surface quickly in customers with embedded proxies)
- Add a preflight step to snapshot configuration of the K8s manifests and docker image digests (we need immutable references)

I've updated the CSV locally to reflect the above; will push a v1.1 if we get the blackout constraints and BGP notes. Also tagging INF-1998 in the Jira link.

Monica
Product Ops — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

(On a side note: if Veridian's IP allowlist will change, we need those CIDRs by EOD Monday.)

From: Tina Lopez <tina.lopez@veridianhealth.com>

Date: 2026-05-23T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patching matrix and night-window ops (proposal + rollback lanes)

Thanks Diego / Monica — quick answers from our side: 

- Blackouts: we have a 00:00–03:00 local blackout on the analytics cluster Friday nights for reporting. The proposed Tue 02:00–05:00 UTC mostly looks okay but can we shift the start to 03:00 UTC to avoid a nightly batch that runs 02:30–03:15 for legacy reporting?
- BGP: We have customer-facing BGP sessions that must not drop for >30s. Our network team requests a staged drain with Graceful shutdown over 90s and active route advertisements to backup peers during full-node evacuations.
- CIDR changes: no planned allowlist changes, current IPs are stable.

If you can absorb the 03:00–06:00 UTC window change, we can confirm on our side. We also asked Raj (vendor) to validate snapshot tooling compatibility with our storage snapshots.

— Tina
SRE Lead, Veridian Health
(Attachment stub referenced: veridian_snapshot_compat.md)

- Net ops: add Graceful drain 90s + active route advertise to backup BGP peer during evacuations; Karthik, I've put a note in INF-1998 requesting a small netops script to run pre/post-drain

I've pushed a v1.1 of the CSV to the Drive link (see related_links) and updated the Jira INF-1998 with the updated window. Please confirm SRE approval and I'll open the dry-run playcall for Wed.

Subject: RE: Private fleet patching matrix and night-window ops (proposal + rollback lanes)

+1 on the updated window and guardrails — engineering signoff below (technical rollback steps):

1) If abort criteria hit during canary: run traffic-steer to v3.1.x fallback variant and pause all further tranche progression
2) If abort criteria persist after fallback: trigger snapshot rollback (storage snapshot) + kube manifest revert (digest pinned) + restart controller with circuit-breaker enabled to prevent auto-fill of KV cache until manual clear
3) Post-rollback verification: run smoke-verify script (smoke-verify.sh) which validates model endpoints, KV sanity, and a 2m inference stability check; success required before resuming traffic
4) Postmortem: capture traces from the disabled canary slice and push timeline to INF-1998 within 24h

I will be on the Wed dry-run bridge and will lead the technical rollback steps. Neha — can you confirm the automation runbook triggers for the snapshot restore path?

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment stub: smoke-verify.sh — referenced in Jira)
